stance_basis: letters protest EO 11644 restrictions but support permit system for legitimate mineral/exploration use
summary: Continental Oil Company submitted two letters from employees in its Minerals Department protesting Executive Order 11644 for limiting off-road vehicle use on public lands without adequate provision for productive uses such as mineral and fossil fuel exploration. Both letters acknowledge that some restrictions on indiscriminate ORV use are appropriate, but argue that a permit system should be established to allow legitimate commercial and exploration users access. No agency response to either letter appears in the document window.
complaint_summary: A geologist from Continental Oil Company's Minerals Department protests EO 11644 for severely limiting ORV use without provision for productive uses like mineral and fossil fuel exploration, while supporting a permit system for legitimate users.

statement.text:
This letter is in protest of Executive Order 11644 which would severly limit the use of off-the-road vehicles on public lands. Although I believe that some restrictions should be placed on off-the-road vehicles to prevent people from indiscriminately tearing up the countryside, little provision has been made for the productive use of such vehicles, such as in the exploration for and development of our mineral and fossil fuel resources.
The proposal that permits be readily available for those people having legitimate reasons for using off-the-road vehicles on public lands is a good one. Thus, constructive use of such vehicles would be encouraged, while at the same time those people obtaining said permits would be more responsible for their actions while using off-the-road vehicles.
